samples.text:
The maps show the town of Seaview on the coast in 1950 and 2020. Overall, the town changed from a small fishing village with farmland to a tourist town with more buildings.

In 1950, there was a hotel in the middle of the town and a church in the east, both next to Coast Road. There was two groups of fishermen's cottages in the west. A pier go into the sea from the beach. In the north there was a big farmland and some trees in the north-east, and a railway was going from west to east across the town.

In 2020, the hotel, the church and the beach are same. The fishermen's cottages were changed to cafés and shops, and the pier is shorter than before. The farmland has been replaced by housing and holiday apartments, and the trees has become a car park. Also, the railway is removed and there is a new road called Hill Road going to north. Finally, a seafront walkway was built along the beach.
samples.why: Overview present though it slightly over-interprets · key changes covered in a basic sequence · mechanical linking · adequate vocabulary · several errors in agreement, articles, tense and word choice that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
The maps illustrate the changes that took place in the coastal town of Seaview between 1950 and 2020. Overall, the town has developed from a fishing settlement surrounded by countryside into a busier, more tourist-oriented resort, while its coastline and a few key buildings have been retained.

Along the coast, the beach and Coast Road remain unchanged, as do the hotel in the centre and the church in the east. However, the two rows of fishermen's cottages in the west have been converted into cafés and shops, and the pier has been shortened. A seafront walkway has also been built running along the entire length of the beach.

The most striking changes are in the north. The large area of farmland has been replaced by housing in the north-west and holiday apartments in the north, while the trees in the north-east have been cut down to create a car park. Moreover, the railway which ran across the town in 1950 has disappeared, and a new road, Hill Road, now leads north from Coast Road, between the apartments and the car park.
samples.why: Clear overview · changes grouped logically into coast and north · effective cohesive devices · good vocabulary (tourist-oriented, converted) · largely error-free sentences with at most a minor slip.

samples.text:
The maps depict Seaview, a coastal town, in 1950 and 2020. Over this seventy-year period, the town evolved from a modest fishing community set among farmland and trees into a tourism-focused resort, with most of its open land developed, while its seafront and principal landmarks were largely retained.

The southern part of the town has kept its essential character. The beach, Coast Road, the hotel and the church are all still in place, but the fishermen's cottages in the west now house cafés and shops, and the pier no longer extends as far out to sea. In addition, a walkway has been laid along the full length of the seafront.

North of the coast road, the transformation has been far more dramatic. The railway that once crossed the town from west to east has been removed altogether, and the extensive farmland beyond it has been built over, with housing in the north-west and a large block of holiday apartments to its east. The woodland in the north-east has been cleared for a car park, and a new route, Hill Road, now runs northwards from Coast Road, separating the apartments from the car park.
samples.why: Perceptive overview of the town's shift in function · clear division between coast and inland changes · sophisticated cohesion · precise vocabulary (evolved, built over, no longer extends) · varied complex structures, error-free.
